# Kacchapajātaka (Ja 215)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kacchapajātaka* (Ja 215) is a verse-narrative of the Pali Jātaka collection belonging to the *Dukanipāta* [Fausböll 1879]. The story opens with the canonical verse incipit *Avadhi vata attānaṁ* and is framed as an account delivered by the Buddha while staying at Jetavana regarding the monk Kokālika, whose ruin was brought about by his uncontrolled speech [Fausböll 1879]. Remarking that Kokālika had similarly suffered destruction due to his talking in a previous existence, the Buddha relates the story of the past, with the fuller background context referenced to the *Mahātakkārijātaka* [Fausböll 1879]. In the story, a talkative tortoise is carried through the air by two geese who hold a stick in their beaks while the tortoise grips the middle with its mouth; provoked by a taunt, the tortoise opens its mouth to speak, loses its grip, and plunges to the ground, splitting in two [Burlingame 1921].

 Scenes identified as the *Kacchapa Jātaka* are also attested in ancient Indian Buddhist sculptural art, such as at Mathurā and on medieval temple plinths [Chauley 1998; Valisinha 1948].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a2) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §1121–1125); Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0502a) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §4553_10–4558)
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database match results for Ja 215 — Identifies text reuse with the Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā and Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā, and confirms lack of cross-language matches.
- [Fausböll 1879] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. 2 (1879) — Provides Pali incipit, title, and commentary framing concerning Kokālika and the Mahātakkārijātaka.
- [Burlingame 1921] Eugene Watson Burlingame, Buddhist Legends: Translated from the Original Pali Text of the Dhammapada Commentary, Part 1 (1921) — Provides alternative title Bahubhāṇijātaka and details the narrative of the tortoise carried by geese and Kokālika.
- [Chauley 1998] G. C. Chauley, Early Buddhist Art in India (1998) — Attests representation of the Kacchapa Jātaka in Mathurā sculpture.
- [Valisinha 1948] Devapriya Valisinha, Buddhist Shrines in India (1948) — Notes depiction of the Kacchapa Jātaka in Indian plinth sculptures.
